# 1 Clement Chapter 43 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 43 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_043_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 43

**43:1** And what wonder is it if those who were entrusted with such a great work in Christ sent forward men of this character, when even the blessed Moses, "a faithful servant in all his house," recorded in the holy writings all that was enjoined upon him?

**43:2** And after him the other prophets followed, bearing witness to the laws he had given.

**43:3** For when rivalry arose concerning the priesthood, and the tribes were disputing among themselves about which of them should be adorned with the glorious name, he commanded the twelve tribal leaders to bring him rods with each tribe's name written on it; and taking them, he bound and sealed them with the signet rings of the tribal leaders, and placed them on the table of God in the tabernacle of testimony.

**43:4** And shutting the tabernacle, he sealed the keys in the same way as the rods.

**43:5** And he said: "Brothers, the tribe whose rod blossoms — this God has chosen to be priests and to minister to him."

**43:6** And when early morning came, he called together all Israel — the six hundred thousand men — and showed the seals to the tribal leaders and opened the tabernacle of testimony and drew out the rods; and the rod of Aaron was found not only to have blossomed, but also to be bearing fruit.

**43:7** What do you think, beloved? Did Moses not know beforehand that this would happen? He certainly knew. But in order that there should be no disorder in Israel, he acted in this way, so that the name of the true and only God might be glorified; to whom be the glory for ever and ever. Amen.

---

## Translator's Note

Chapter 43 retells the Numbers 17 narrative of Aaron's rod as a precedent for the legitimate, divinely-validated appointment of priestly leaders against rival claimants. The typological application is clear: just as Moses used an orderly procedure (the rods with names, sealed and witnessed) to resolve the rivalry over the priesthood — and God validated his chosen leader through miraculous blossoming — so the apostles' appointment of bishops was orderly, divinely-guided, and should not be overturned by rivals. The quote "a faithful servant in all his house" (v. 1) echoes Numbers 12:7 (also Hebrews 3:5). The detail of "six hundred thousand men" (v. 6) comes from the census numbers of Exodus/Numbers. SOPHIA follows LOGOS in "tabernacle of testimony" and "signet rings" for technical precision.

---

*SOPHIA represents the consensus translation, balancing literalness and clarity.*
